mainTopic: Narrowing a wide מבוי, the rules of עומד and פרוץ (including the רב דימי–רבין dispute), and צורת הפתח
overview: The גמרא explains how to narrow a מבוי whose entrance is wider than ten אמות. One way is to stand a board lengthwise down the alley. Another way follows רב יהודה: put a three-אמה board two אמות from the wall, which leaves an opening of exactly ten. The גמרא asks why other board arrangements were not suggested and tries to learn rules about עומד מרובה על הפרוץ and עומד כפרוץ. Each proof is rejected: a small board with open air on both sides is cancelled, and some setups are simply more work than the רבנן required. Next the גמרא worries that people will use the small gap instead of the main entrance. רב אדא בר מתנה answers that people do not leave a big entrance for a small one unless it saves them walking. The גמרא then brings a טומאה source about a leather seat and its hole, reported differently by רב דימי and רבין. אביי and רב דימי debate whether they truly disagree, and the dispute is narrowed to פרוץ כעומד. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה: a צורת הפתח fixes a too-wide entrance, and the discussion of width and height continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First method: a board set lengthwise down the alley
steps.stepSummary: To narrow a wide מבוי, you set a board ten טפחים high and four אמות long down the length of the alley, splitting it into two narrower alleys.
steps.simpleTranslation: One makes a board ten handbreadths high and four cubits long, and stands it along the length of the alleyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a method for fixing a מבוי that is too wide: put a tall board down the middle so the one wide entrance becomes two narrow ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מבוי wider than ten אמות cannot be fixed with a normal לחי or קורה. The board does not shrink the entrance from the side. Instead it divides the alley lengthwise, so each half is ten אמות or less. It must be ten טפחים high and four אמות long so that it counts as a real dividing wall.

keyTerms.meaning: A board or wall-section set up as a partition
Ten טפחים (handbreadths) high, the minimum height of a halachic wall
Along the length of the alleyway

steps.confusionAlert: The board does not stand across the entrance. It runs lengthwise into the alley, like a divider, turning one wide alley into two narrow ones.

phrases.english: One makes a board ten handbreadths high
with a length of four cubits,
and stands it along the length of the alleyway.
phrases.notes: This creates two smaller alleyways at the entrance, each no wider than ten cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹשֶׂה פַּס גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה בְּמֶשֶׁךְ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion, on the previous amud, of how to narrow an over-wide מבוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A board ten טפחים high and four אמות long, placed lengthwise in the מבוי, divides it and solves the width problem.

steps.title: Second method: רב יהודה's three-cubit board
steps.stepSummary: Following רב יהודה, a fifteen-אמה-wide מבוי is narrowed by leaving two אמות of space from the wall and putting up a three-אמה board, which leaves an opening of exactly ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else, follow רב יהודה. He said: if an alley is fifteen cubits wide, one moves two cubits away from the wall and makes a board three cubits wide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to narrow the מבוי. This one follows a ruling of רב יהודה about a fifteen-אמה-wide alley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The numbers work out like this: 2 (gap) + 3 (board) + 10 (opening) = 15. The board counts even though it does not touch the wall. The board is three אמות and the gap is only two, so the solid part is bigger than the open part. That is the rule of עומד מרובה על הפרוץ: when more is standing than open, the whole section counts as closed.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with רב יהודה's ruling

steps.whyThisMatters: The exact numbers in רב יהודה's case set up the question in the next step: why only this arrangement, and not another one that also adds up to fifteen?

phrases.english: Alternatively, like Rav Yehuda,
for Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: מָבוֹי שֶׁהוּא רָחָב חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה —
phrases.english: An alleyway that is fifteen cubits wide —
he distances two cubits from the wall
and makes a board of three cubits.
phrases.notes: 2 + 3 = 5 cubits are dealt with, leaving an opening of 10 cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי כִּדְרַב יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second method for the same goal of narrowing the מבוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a fifteen-אמה מבוי, a three-אמה board placed two אמות from the wall reduces the opening to ten.

steps.title: Why not two smaller boards? An inference about standing versus open sections
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב יהודה did not allow two boards of one and a half אמות each with a two-אמה gap between them. It tries to prove from this that standing parts on two sides of a gap do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let him make a board of one and a half cubits, leave two cubits, and make another board of one and a half cubits. We can learn from this: if the standing part is bigger than the open part only by counting both sides of the gap, it does not count as standing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב יהודה chose this particular arrangement. It then tries to draw a general rule from the fact that he did not mention a different arrangement that seems to work just as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other arrangement is: wall, 1.5 board, 2 gap, 1.5 board, then the 10 opening. Here the standing parts total 3, which is more than the 2-אמה gap, but only when you add both sides of the gap together. רב יהודה did not mention this option. So the גמרא infers that עומד מרובה על הפרוץ only works when the standing part is on one side of the gap, not split across two sides.

keyTerms.meaning: And why? (asking about an apparently unnecessary requirement)
Learn from this; conclude from here
The standing part is bigger than the open part, so the section counts as closed

steps.confusionAlert: Both arrangements use 3 אמות of board and a 2-אמה gap. The only difference is that רב יהודה's board is one piece on one side, while the other option splits it into two pieces, one on each side of the gap.

phrases.english: But why?
Let him make a board of a cubit and a half,
and leave a space of two cubits,
and make another board of a cubit and a half.
Learn from this:
standing that is greater than the breach
only from two sides is not considered standing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רב יהודה's specific setup and draws a general principle from what he left out.
steps.raayaObject: עומד מרובה על הפרוץ does not apply when the standing parts must be combined from both sides of the gap.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's silence about the 1.5 + 2 + 1.5 arrangement, which would otherwise seem valid.

steps.title: Rejection: here the air on both sides cancels the far board
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Standing parts on two sides of a gap normally do count, but in this case the second small board is surrounded by open air on both sides, which cancels it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, I can tell you that it does count as standing. But this case is different: the open air on this side and the open air on that side come together and cancel the board.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the previous step. It explains that רב יהודה skipped the two-board option for a different reason, not because standing parts on two sides never combine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second 1.5-אמה board has a 2-אמה gap on one side and the 10-אמה opening on the other. Since it is surrounded by open air on both sides, that air cancels it, so it cannot count as part of the wall. The general principle of עומד מרובה על הפרוץ from two sides is left standing. Only this particular setup fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you (opening a rejection)

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה's method uses one three-אמה board with a two-אמה gap from the wall. The proof that standing parts on two sides of a gap never combine is rejected. The two-board setup fails only because the far board is caught between open air on both sides.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the general rule that standing parts on both sides of a gap can combine. It adds one limit: a small board with open space on both sides is cancelled.

phrases.english: Actually, I can tell you that it is considered standing,
but here is different,
since the air of this side comes
phrases.notes: The 2-cubit gap next to the far board.

phrases.english: and the air of that side
phrases.notes: The 10-cubit opening on the board's other side.

phrases.english: and cancels it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ הָוֵי עוֹמֵד, וְשָׁאנֵי הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the general conclusion that עומד מרובה על הפרוץ from two sides never counts.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof ignored that the far 1.5-אמה board is surrounded by open air on both sides, and that air cancels it. That, not the general principle, is why רב יהודה did not suggest the two-board option.

steps.title: Three one-אמה boards, and a proof that equal standing and open is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another arrangement: three boards of one אמה each, with one-אמה gaps between them. Since רב יהודה did not suggest it, the גמרא tries to prove that עומד כפרוץ is אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him make a one-אמה board and leave a one-אמה gap, make another one-אמה board and leave a one-אמה gap, and make a third one-אמה board. Learn from this: when the standing part equals the open part, it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way to narrow the מבוי using three small boards. Because רב יהודה did not mention it, the גמרא tries to prove that a wall which is half standing and half open does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three boards of one אמה plus two gaps of one אמה take up five אמות, which leaves the needed ten-אמה opening. In this setup every gap is exactly as wide as the boards beside it, which is the case of עומד כפרוץ. If that worked, רב יהודה should have allowed it, so his silence seems to show that עומד כפרוץ is אסור.

keyTerms.meaning: A board or post set up to form part of a partition
He should leave a space (literally, distance)
Where the standing part of a partition equals the open part

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 3. There the question was about two boards with a gap between them. Here the issue is a specific ratio: the standing parts exactly EQUAL the open parts.

phrases.english: Let him make a board of one cubit and leave a gap of one cubit,
phrases.notes: Measured out from the wall of the alley

phrases.english: and make another board of one cubit and leave another gap of one cubit,
and make a third board of one cubit.
phrases.notes: Total: 5 cubits, leaving an opening of 10

phrases.english: Learn from this:
standing equal to breached is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same method as step 3. It offers another arrangement רב יהודה could have suggested and draws a new inference from his silence.
steps.raayaObject: That עומד כפרוץ (standing equal to breached) is אסור
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's choice of a single three-אמה board instead of three one-אמה boards

steps.title: The surrounding open air cancels the boards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. עומד כפרוץ really is מותר, but here the open air on both sides of the boards cancels them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I can tell you that it is permitted. But here is different, because the open air on this side and the open air on that side come together and cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Equal standing and open sections are normally fine, but this particular setup fails for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule of עומד כפרוץ stays מותר. The problem is the far board: it has a one-אמה gap on one side and the ten-אמה opening on the other. It is no wider than the gap beside it, so the air on both sides 'swallows' it and it no longer counts as a partition. This is the same reasoning the גמרא used in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you (opens a rejection that keeps the original position)

phrases.english: Really, I can tell you: it is permitted,
but here it is different, because the open air comes
from this side and from that side
and cancels it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ מוּתָּר וְשָׁאנֵי הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 5 by applying the same reasoning as step 4 (air on both sides cancels the board) to explain why רב יהודה avoided that arrangement.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the inference about עומד כפרוץ. It agrees that the three-board setup does not work.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The setup fails because open air surrounds the boards and cancels them, not because עומד כפרוץ is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the general rule that עומד כפרוץ is מותר. A failure in one special case does not overturn the general category.

steps.title: Why not two boards of one and a half אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another arrangement: leave a one-אמה gap, put up a one-and-a-half-אמה board, leave another one-אמה gap, and put up another one-and-a-half-אמה board.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him leave a gap of one אמה and make a board of one and a half אמות, then leave a gap of one אמה and make another board of one and a half אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers yet another way to narrow the מבוי and implicitly asks why רב יהודה did not mention it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One plus one and a half plus one plus one and a half equals five אמות, which leaves the ten-אמה opening. Here each board (one and a half) is wider than each gap (one), so the problem of עומד כפרוץ does not come up. So why did רב יהודה insist on a single three-אמה board?

phrases.aramaic: וְיַרְחִיק אַמָּה וְיַעֲשֶׂה פַּס אַמָּה וּמֶחֱצָה,
phrases.english: Let him leave a gap of one cubit and make a board of a cubit and a half,

phrases.aramaic: וְיַרְחִיק אַמָּה וְיַעֲשֶׂה פַּס אַמָּה וּמֶחֱצָה.
phrases.english: and leave another gap of one cubit and make another board of a cubit and a half.
phrases.notes: Total: 5 cubits, leaving an opening of 10

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיַרְחִיק אַמָּה וְיַעֲשֶׂה פַּס אַמָּה וּמֶחֱצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 6 explained the failure of the three-board plan, this offers a plan where the standing parts are larger than the open parts.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's method of a single three-אמה board with a two-אמה gap from the wall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This arrangement seems valid, since standing is greater than open. רב יהודה should have mentioned it as another option.

steps.title: It would work, but the רבנן did not demand that much effort
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the two-board arrangement would work. רב יהודה gave the simpler method because the רבנן did not burden a person with making extra boards.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so. But the רבנן did not trouble him with all this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the suggestion is correct and valid. רב יהודה simply described the easiest way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no problem with the law here. Two boards of one and a half אמות would work just as well. רב יהודה taught the one-board method because it is less work, and the רבנן did not require the harder setup when the easier one is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (agreeing with the suggestion)

steps.whatToRemember: To narrow a fifteen-אמה מבוי, one three-אמה board two אמות from the wall is the easiest method. Two boards of one and a half אמות with one-אמה gaps would also work. עומד כפרוץ stays מותר in general, but small boards surrounded by open air on both sides are cancelled.

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so,
but the Sages did not trouble him this much.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי וְכוּלֵּי הַאי לָא אַטְרְחוּהּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by agreeing with it and explaining why רב יהודה chose the simpler method.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the alternative works, but the easier method was given so as not to burden people
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's silence meant the two-board method is invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two-board method is valid. רב יהודה just gave the least burdensome option.

steps.title: Worry that people will use the small opening instead of the big one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא worries that people might stop using the large entrance and start entering through the small opening, which would cancel the main entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we should worry that a person might leave the big entrance and go in through the small entrance!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with רב יהודה's arrangement, which leaves a two-אמה gap next to the ten-אמה entrance. If people start walking in through the small two-אמה opening, the big opening might stop counting as the real entrance of the מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The big entrance is the one with the proper side post, which is what makes carrying in the מבוי allowed. If the small opening becomes the main way in, the big opening loses its status as the entrance. Then the מבוי would no longer have a proper entrance, and carrying would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us worry about, be concerned that

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps he will leave the big entrance,
and enter through the small entrance!
phrases.notes: If that happens, the big entrance stops counting as the entrance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having settled רב יהודה's method in steps 2–8, raises a practical problem with it: its two-אמה gap sits next to the ten-אמה main entrance.
steps.kashyaTarget: The arrangement that leaves a small opening alongside the large main entrance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If people use the small opening, the large opening loses its status as the entrance, and the מבוי becomes forbidden for carrying.

steps.title: People do not leave a big entrance to use a small one
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה answers with a חזקה: a person does not leave a large entrance to go through a small one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנה said: We can assume that a person does not leave a big entrance and go in through a small entrance.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנה answers the worry. We can rely on normal human behavior: people prefer the big entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה is a safe assumption based on how people usually act. Since people naturally use the wide entrance, the big entrance keeps its status. So the small opening does not cause a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A safe assumption based on normal behavior

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said:

phrases.aramaic: חֲזָקָה אֵין אָדָם מַנִּיחַ פֶּתַח גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: It is a presumption that a person does not leave a big entrance
and enter through a small entrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה: חֲזָקָה אֵין אָדָם מַנִּיחַ פֶּתַח גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to a חזקה about normal human behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: People might switch to the small opening and cancel the big entrance.
steps.terutzMaskana: People naturally use the big entrance, so it keeps its status.

steps.title: Why is this different from רבי אמי and רבי אסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this case is different from the ruling of רבי אמי and רבי אסי, who were worried about a side breach near the entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difference between this and the ruling of רבי אמי and רבי אסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given. רבי אמי and רבי אסי forbid carrying when a מבוי has a breach on its side near the entrance, so they seem to worry that people will use a smaller opening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people never leave a big entrance for a small one, a side breach should not be a problem either. But רבי אמי and רבי אסי do treat it as a problem. So the חזקה of רב אדא בר מתנה seems to contradict their ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Two אמוראים who ruled about a side breach near the entrance of a מבוי

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מִדְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי וּדְרַבֵּי אַסִּי?
phrases.english: And what is different from the ruling of Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi?
phrases.notes: They forbid carrying when there is a breach on the side of the מבוי near its entrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מִדְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי וּדְרַבֵּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חזקה from step 10 using another ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חזקה of רב אדא בר מתנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אמי and רבי אסי worry that people will use a side breach, which suggests people do sometimes leave the big entrance.

steps.title: A shortcut makes the difference
steps.stepSummary: In רבי אמי and רבי אסי's case the side breach is a shortcut, so people use it. Here the small opening is not a shortcut, so people stay with the big entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it shortens his walk. Here, it does not shorten his walk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The two cases are different because of walking distance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A side breach lets someone coming from the side cut the walk short, so people really might use it. In our case both openings are at the front of the מבוי, so the small one saves no walking. With no shortcut, people stick to the big entrance, and the חזקה holds.
steps.whatToRemember: A person does not leave a big entrance for a small one, unless the small one saves walking distance.

phrases.english: There, it shortens his walking.
phrases.notes: The side breach is a shortcut for someone coming from the side.

phrases.english: Here, it does not shorten his walking.
phrases.notes: Both openings are at the front, so the small one saves nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by showing the cases are different.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אמי and רבי אסי contradict the חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חזקה applies only when the small opening gives no shortcut; a side breach does give one.

steps.title: A stool's leather and its hole combine to make a טפח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a teaching from the laws of טומאה: the leather of a stool and the hole in it combine to reach the size of a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: The leather of a stool and its hole join together to make a טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new source from the laws of טומאת אוהל. It is setting up the next move, which returns to the question of a standing part that is bigger than the open part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A covering must be at least a טפח wide to spread טומאה from a dead body to what is underneath. This teaching says that a stool's leather and the hole in it are counted together to reach a טפח. The coming steps will ask exactly when an open space can be counted together with solid material.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in another place (in a different מסכת)
The leather covering of a stool
Join together, combine to make a measure
A handbreadth, the minimum size of an אוהל for טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic dropped out of nowhere. The גמרא is bringing a טומאה source to shed light on the earlier question about standing parts and open parts in a wall.

phrases.english: We learned there:
The leather of a stool and its hole —
join together to make a handbreadth.
phrases.notes: This matters for טומאת אוהל, where a covering of one טפח spreads טומאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the entrance discussion and brings a new source that will connect back to the question of עומד and פרוץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leather of a stool and its hole combine to complete the measure of a טפח for טומאת אוהל.

steps.title: What is the leather of a stool?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the עור העסלא from the earlier teaching actually is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'leather of the stool'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to define a word from the teaching in Step 13. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that leather and its hole combine to make a טפח depends on knowing what object we are talking about. So the גמרא first asks for a clear definition.

phrases.english: What is 'the leather of the stool'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a term used in the טומאה teaching of Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What object the term עור העסלא refers to.

steps.title: It is the leather cover of a toilet seat
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה, quoting רבי יוחנן, explains that it is the leather cover of a toilet seat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it is the leather cover of a toilet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a definition: it is the leather seat cover of a toilet, which has a hole in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we can see why there is a hole: a toilet seat must have an opening. That is why the leather and the hole need to combine to reach a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who quotes רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
The leather covering of a toilet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עור העסלא is the leather cover of a toilet seat.

steps.title: How big can the hole be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what size the hole and leather can be and still combine to a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact measurements of the leather and the hole. This sets up two reports from the Land of Israel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hole were huge, it would not make sense to count it as part of the leather. So there must be a limit on how much of the טפח can be hole.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much? (asking for a measurement)

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the object, the גמרא asks for its measurements.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size limits of the leather and hole that still combine to a טפח.

steps.title: רב דימי's measurement: two, two, and two
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports: two fingers of leather on each side and a two-finger hole in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from the Land of Israel, he said: two fingers here, two fingers here, and a two-finger space in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives the first answer: 2 fingers of leather, a 2-finger hole, and 2 more fingers of leather, 6 fingers in total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here each leather side is only equal to the hole, not bigger. Only when you add both sides together (4) is the leather more than the hole (2).

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from the Land of Israel to Bavel)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
Two fingers from here, and two fingers from here,
and two fingers of space in the middle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the measurement question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 2 fingers leather, 2 fingers hole, 2 fingers leather.

steps.title: רבין's measurement: one and a half, one and a half, and one
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports: one and a half fingers of leather on each side and a one-finger hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: a finger and a half here, a finger and a half here, and a one-finger space in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין brings a different report of the same measurement: 1.5 + 1 + 1.5, which is 4 fingers in total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבין's version each leather side on its own (1.5) is already bigger than the hole (1). This difference becomes the key point in Step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who also brought teachings from the Land of Israel

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: אֶצְבַּע וּמֶחֱצָה מִכָּאן, וְאֶצְבַּע וּמֶחֱצָה מִכָּאן,
phrases.english: A finger and a half from here, and a finger and a half from here,
and one finger of space in the middle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different report of the measurement given in Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 1.5 fingers leather, 1 finger hole, 1.5 fingers leather.

steps.title: אביי asks: do you two really disagree?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב דימי whether he and רבין truly disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב דימי: Do you disagree with each other?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי notices the two reports give different numbers and asks whether this is a real argument. This sets up רב דימי's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two totals look different (6 against 4). אביי wants to know if they are two opinions or the same rule described in two ways.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Dimi:
Do you disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב דִּימִי: מִי פְּלִיגִיתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two reports from Steps 17 and 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב דימי and רבין hold different rules.

steps.title: רב דימי: no argument, just different finger sizes
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי says they agree: רבין measured with thumbs and he measured with small fingers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. This one is in large fingers, and this one is in small fingers, and we do not disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי explains that both reports describe one טפח. רבין counted in thumbs (4 per טפח) and רב דימי counted in small fingers (6 per טפח).
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this is right, the different numbers are only different units of measurement. The real size of the leather and the hole would be the same in both reports.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up: the 'large' fingers go with רבין's smaller numbers (4 thumbs), and the 'small' fingers go with רב דימי's larger numbers (6 small fingers).

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
this one is with large fingers, this one is with small fingers,
and they do not disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, הָא — בְּרַבְרְבָתָא, הָא — בְּזוּטְרָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question by explaining the difference away.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reports use different finger sizes but describe the same טפח.

steps.title: אביי: you do disagree about adding up two sides
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the 'same size' answer. רב דימי and רבין disagree about whether standing sections on both sides of a gap may be added together to outweigh it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No, you do disagree, and you disagree about 'standing is more than breached' from two sides. For you, it counts as standing even from two sides. For רבין, from one side it counts as standing, but from two sides it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי says the difference is real. In רב דימי's version you must add both leather sides to beat the hole, while in רבין's version one side alone beats the hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רב דימי, each side (2) only equals the hole (2), so he must hold that two sides may combine. With רבין, each side (1.5) is bigger than the hole (1), which shows he needs one side alone to be bigger. This is the rule of עומד מרובה על הפרוץ, which also applies to walls and partitions.

keyTerms.meaning: The standing part is more than the open (breached) part
From two sides (adding both sides together)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי claims the dispute is about adding standing parts from two sides. רב דימי pushes back on this in step 23, and step 24 narrows the dispute to פרוץ כעומד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties a small טומאה detail back to the main topic of עירובין: when a wall with gaps still counts as a wall.

phrases.english: He said to him: Not so, you do disagree,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְעוֹמֵד מְרוּבֶּה עַל הַפָּרוּץ מִשְׁתֵּי רוּחוֹת פְּלִיגִיתוּ.
phrases.english: and you disagree about 'standing greater than breached' from two sides.
According to you, it counts as standing even from two sides,
according to Ravin, from one side it counts as standing,
from two sides it does not count as standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב דימי's claim in Step 20 that there is no argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the two reports differ only in finger size.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ratio of each side to the hole is different in the two reports (2:2 against 1.5:1), so the difference is real and not only about units.

steps.title: אביי proves the two reports are not the same
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows that if רבין agreed with רב דימי, he would have given different numbers.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think you two don't disagree, then רבין should have said: one and a third fingers of leather on this side, one and a third on that side, and a one-and-a-third-finger hole in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי backs up his claim that רב דימי and רבין really disagree. He points out that רבין's numbers do not match רב דימי's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי's case has three equal parts: side, hole, side. In רבין's larger 'thumb' fingers, three equal parts would be 1⅓ each. רבין instead made the hole smaller than each side (1½, 1, 1½), so he seems to need each side to be bigger than the hole by itself. That is a real disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: For if it enters your mind (if you were to think)

steps.confusionAlert: Two kinds of 'finger' are in play: a thumb-width, which is bigger, and a small-finger width. Four thumbs and six small fingers both equal one טפח. So 1⅓ thumbs on each of three parts equals 2 small fingers on each part, which is רב דימי's case.

phrases.english: For if it should enter your mind that you do not disagree,
Ravin should have said as follows:
a finger and a third from here,
and a finger and a third from here,
and a finger and a third of space in the middle.
phrases.notes: All three parts are equal, matching רב דימי's 2-2-2 in small fingers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof behind אביי's rejection in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That רב דימי and רבין truly disagree.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבין's choice of numbers. If the two agreed, he would have described three equal parts of 1⅓ thumbs.

steps.title: רב דימי pushes back that a big dispute doesn't fit either
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי argues that if he really held that both sides add together, he would have given a much more dramatic example.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what are you saying, that we disagree? Then I should have said: one and two-thirds fingers of leather on this side, one and two-thirds on that side, and a hole of two and two-thirds fingers in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers אביי. He says the numbers don't support a big disagreement either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב דימי held that the two sides add together against the hole, his best example would have a hole much bigger than each side, such as 1⅔, 2⅔, 1⅔ (still six small fingers in total). He gave equal parts instead. So his opinion is not that broad.

keyTerms.meaning: According to me, for my view

phrases.english: Rather, what — we disagree?
If so, for me, I should have said as follows:
a finger and two thirds from here,
and a finger and two thirds from here,
and two fingers and two thirds of space in the middle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses אביי's own method from step 22 against the broad version of the dispute.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the dispute is about adding the sides together in general.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If רב דימי held the broad view, he would have picked a case where the hole is clearly bigger than each side.

steps.title: The real dispute: a gap exactly equal to the standing part
steps.stepSummary: If they disagree at all, the dispute is only about a case of פרוץ כעומד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is room to say that we disagree, we disagree about a breached part that is equal to the standing part.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי narrows the disagreement to one specific case. This settles what the two reports are really about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the hole is exactly as wide as each side, רב דימי counts it as standing, which is why his three parts are equal. רבין counts it as breached, so he needs each side to be bigger than the hole. Neither holds that the two sides add together to outweigh a bigger gap.

keyTerms.meaning: If there is room to say
A gap equal in size to the standing part

steps.whatToRemember: רב דימי and רבין disagree only about פרוץ כעומד. רב דימי says an equal gap counts as standing, and רבין says it counts as breached.
steps.whyThisMatters: פרוץ כעומד is a key question in the laws of walls and partitions throughout מסכת עירובין.

phrases.english: Rather, if there is room to say that we disagree —
we disagree about a breach equal to the standing part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the back-and-forth of steps 21–23 by naming the narrow point of dispute.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute is only about פרוץ כעומד: רב דימי treats it as standing, and רבין treats it as breached.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: a doorway frame fixes a wide entrance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: with a צורת הפתח, an entrance wider than ten אמות does not need narrowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it has the form of a doorway, even though it is wider than ten, it does not need to be narrowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the side discussion and goes back to the משנה. It quotes the rule that a צורת הפתח solves the problem of a too-wide alleyway entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an alleyway entrance wider than ten אמות must be narrowed before a קורה or לחי can work. A צורת הפתח (two posts with a crossbar) turns the opening into a 'doorway', so its width no longer matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Form of a doorway: two upright posts with a beam across the top

phrases.english: If it has the form of a doorway,
even though it is wider than ten —
it does not need to be narrowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by returning to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צורת הפתח makes an alleyway entrance valid even when it is wider than ten אמות.

steps.title: Doorway frame helps width, cornice helps height
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes what each solution is known to fix: צורת הפתח fixes width and אמלתרא fixes height.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found that a doorway frame works for its width, and a cornice works for its height.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up two known rules: one solution for width and one for height. This is a setup line, preparing a question about whether each solution also works for the other measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know from the משנה that a צורת הפתח fixes an entrance that is too wide. From earlier we know that an אמלתרא fixes a קורה that is too high, above twenty אמות. Pairing them this way invites the next question about crossing them over.

keyTerms.meaning: A decorative cornice or molding on the beam

phrases.english: We have found a doorway form that is effective for its width,
and a cornice that is effective for its height.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה line in step 25 and sets up the next inquiry.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צורת הפתח is known to work for width, and אמלתרא is known to work for height.
